output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: LoggerRequestProcessor.process() passed viewLogRequest.getPath() (and the equivalent paths for the other three log commands) straight into file I/O (LoggerUtils.readWholeFileContent / FileInputStream / Files.lines / File.delete) with no validation, so a request path like <base>/logs/../secret.txt read files outside the log directory.

Fix: Added private checkPathSecurity(String path) in LoggerRequestProcessor. It rejects null/empty paths and any path whose raw or normalized form contains a ".." parent-directory segment, throwing IllegalArgumentException (consistent with the existing default-case behavior) and logging the rejection. The check is invoked for all four path-bearing command types (GET_LOG_BYTES_REQUEST, VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST, ROLL_VIEW_LOG_REQUEST, REMOVE_TAK_LOG_REQUEST) before any file access, so no marker-bearing content is read/returned for a traversal path.

Also added a regression test testProcessViewWholeLogRequestPathTraversal() to the existing LoggerRequestProcessorTest that asserts a "../"-containing path throws IllegalArgumentException. Verified the module builds and both the new test and the pre-existing legitimate-path test pass (TEST_RC=0); the traversal attempt is logged and blocked.
output_json.risk_notes: Legitimate log paths in DolphinScheduler are absolute paths built from process/task IDs (e.g. .../logs/<code>/<version>/<procInstId>/<taskId>.log) and never contain ".." segments, so normal log viewing/removal is unaffected (verified by the existing "/log/path" test still passing). Behavior change: a malicious/malformed path now throws IllegalArgumentException instead of silently reading; this surfaces as an error to the remote caller rather than returned file content, which is the intended hardening. The check is a conservative ".."-rejection rather than a full base-directory confinement, chosen to stay minimal and match the validated POV; it does not restrict to a configured root, but it fully blocks the demonstrated traversal vector.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in LoggerRequestProcessor by validating the attacker-controlled log path before it is used for any file operation (view whole log, get log bytes, roll view log, remove task log). A new checkPathSecurity() helper normalizes the path and rejects any request containing a parent-directory ("..") segment, blocking arbitrary file reads outside the intended log directory.
